facts.text: The environment is registered under the id 'cartpole' with entry point 'safe_control_gym.envs.gym_control.cartpole:CartPole'
CartPole extends BenchmarkEnv, the benchmark's base gymnasium environment
CartPole is a physics-based environment that uses PyBullet
The action space is a one-element Box with low -10 and high 10; the physical action bounds are also -10 and 10 and the action unit is N unless normalized_rl_action_space is set
A control action is denormalized when needed, disturbed, and clipped to the physical action bounds before it is applied
The state and observation labels are x, x_dot, theta and theta_dot with units m, m/s, rad and rad/s
The state and observation spaces are Box spaces bounded by +-4.8 for x, +-20 for x_dot, +-pi for theta and +-20 for theta_dot; the state bound is twice the failure threshold
The failure thresholds are +-2.4 for the cart position and +-90 degrees (pi/2 rad) for the pole angle
The stabilization goal tolerance is 0.05 in the state norm
The episode terminates when the cart position or the pole angle passes its threshold, or when the stabilization goal is reached
The default reward is the exponential of the negative quadratic state error plus an action penalty, so it lies in (0, 1]
The default physics and control frequencies are both 50 Hz
The control timestep is 1/ctrl_freq = 0.02 s and the physics timestep is 1/pyb_freq; the default frequencies give one physics step per control step
The default episode length is 5 s
after_step marks the episode done at the control-step limit and records info['TimeLimit.truncated'] when it was not already done
The initial state is randomized by default (randomized_init=True)
The initial-state randomization draws x, x_dot, theta and theta_dot uniformly from (-0.05, 0.05)
BenchmarkEnv.seed seeds numpy's generator and the action space and returns the seed
reset accepts an optional seed and passes it to before_reset, which reseeds when it is not None
step returns the legacy (observation, reward, done, info) tuple; done covers failure, goal and the time limit

determinism.notes: cap.world.seed.v1 sets the seed of the next reset and cap.world.reset.v1 accepts a seed; the dynamics are deterministic for a fixed seed and action sequence.  This package's fake draws initial states with Python's random.Random and upstream draws them from numpy's generator, so one seed gives different trajectories on the two

gaps: the fake backend is a two-link rigid-body approximation with a force input, not PyBullet: the upstream URDF contact, damping, inertia and PyBullet solver behaviour are not modelled, and the fake was never compared with the upstream environment
no actuator, sensor, noise or disturbance model: the force is an ideal clipped input and no observation or action disturbance is applied
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, so ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms (20 ms) only
no rendering, GUI, video recording, symbolic model, constraint evaluation or adversarial control
snapshot and restore are not offered: the upstream environment exposes no get_state/set_state pair

the fake draws initial states with Python's random.Random while upstream uses numpy's generator, and the fake returns the modern five-tuple while upstream returns the legacy four-tuple, so one seed gives different trajectories on the two

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop the runtime refuses step, reset and seed calls until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, and the last state stays readable
